transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, well, what made me come in is that I've been having some trouble at work lately. I'm a receptionist, and I've started losing my place while I’m scheduling appointments or working on the lobby displays. It's like... my mind just slips off track because I’m busy thinking about what I might have overlooked.
When you lose your place at work, are you usually getting stuck on the same unwanted thought over and over, like that you might have missed or done something wrong?

Yeah, that's exactly what happens. I mean, I can tell myself, 'Sunny, it’s handled,' but the thought just keeps looping anyway. And then... well, pretty soon I’ve gone from that one concern to another, until I’m just checking details in my head over and over again.
When those thoughts get stuck, do you feel driven to do something repeatedly to make sure things are okay?

No, not really. I don't feel like I have to actually do anything physical to fix it. Like, I'm not getting up to check the computer or the lobby displays over and over. It really just stays in my head. I just get stuck thinking about the details, but I don't have a specific action I feel forced to do.
Do these thoughts feel intrusive—like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

No, I wouldn't say they pop in out of nowhere. It's more like... I'll just be thinking about my day or my tasks, and then I start worrying about one thing, and it just snowballs from there. It's not like an unwanted thought just forces its way in, I just kind of slide into worrying about it.
Do you find yourself worrying like this about a lot of different parts of your life, not just work?

Yeah, I do. It's definitely not just work. I find myself worrying about all kinds of ordinary things now. Like... paying the bills, or travel plans, or even just little paperwork errors. It just feels like one small mix-up could somehow turn into a much bigger problem, so my mind just kind of latches onto those things.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control the worry?

Yeah, it is. I try to stop it. I can tell myself, 'Sunny, it's handled,' but the thought just keeps looping. And pretty soon, I've gone from one concern to another, and I just end up checking all the details in my head over and over again. I just can't seem to turn it off once it starts.
About how long have you been worrying like this most days?

I'd say it's been going on for about nine months now. It really started ever since... well, I had this overnight detention, and there was a whole paperwork mix-up around it. Ever since that happened, I've just been worrying like this most days.
When you’ve been worrying, do you often feel physically tense?

Yeah, definitely. Um, at the front desk I can still smile and help people and do my job, but inside... I just feel wound tight. It's like my shoulders are up around my ears all day, and I'm just constantly waiting for something to go wrong.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yeah, I think that's kind of what I meant a second ago. That feeling of being wound tight... it's exactly like being on edge. Even when I look fine and I'm smiling at the front desk, inside I just feel restless. I can't really settle down because, like I said, I'm just constantly bracing myself for something to go wrong.
Do you find yourself getting irritable more easily than usual?
No, not really. I don't think I've been snapping at anyone or feeling more irritable than normal. It's mostly just that internal tension I mentioned.
Do you often feel tired easily?
No, not really. I mean, I get tired at the end of the day after working a full shift, but I wouldn't say I get tired easily. My energy levels during the day are pretty normal.
Do you often have trouble concentrating because your mind goes blank or gets pulled into your worries?

Yes, actually. That’s kind of what made me finally come in to see someone. I’ve started losing my place while I’m at work. Like, I'll be scheduling appointments or working on the lobby displays, and my mind just... slips off track. It's mostly because I'm busy thinking about what I might have overlooked instead of what's right in front of me.
Do these worries often make it hard for you to fall asleep or stay asleep?

Yes, they do. Most nights I get into bed feeling pretty tired, but then I just lie there. I end up going over tomorrow’s appointments in my head, or worrying about some form I might have missed at the front desk. And even when I do manage to fall asleep, I usually wake up feeling like I never really settled.
